newsitem.title: USA: USWC crudes up with WTI, discount stays idle.
newsitem.headline: USWC crudes up with WTI, discount stays idle.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices climbed Tuesday with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) values, while discounts were flat as traders tried to confirm an Alaskan crude deal that went unreported last week.
Most West Coast crude buyers were angered by a rumor that BP secretly sold a second cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude last week at a discount wider than $1.05.
BP and Exxon denied selling the cargo, but U.S. Oil, the alleged buyer, declined to comment when asked if they purchased the crude.
Outright ANS rose 10 cents to $18.23/18.43 a barrel.

One refinery trader said U.S. Oil declined their offer of Colombian South Blend crude because they had bought the cargo of ANS. The trader said U.S. Oil could have bought the cargo at $1.10 below WTI or wider.
"We know it was wider than $1.10. It's the indications were getting," he said.
In Canada, two shut pipelines on IPL Energy's pipeline into the U.S. began flowing at low rates Tuesday after power was restored to two pumping stations in the U.S. Midwest.
West Coast traders watched the situation to see if the shutdowns would force excess crude to the Pacific Northwest.
A 2,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) shipment for California heavy grade in May sold at postings Tuesday, traders said.
